featured.title: Martin Luther in 5 Latin Phrases
featured.summary: Jesus’s perfect life and sacrificial death count for all believers. So God’s righteousness isn’t merely his judgment. It’s also his gift.
featured.summary_zh: 马丁·路德于1483年11月10日生于德国艾斯莱本. 第二天他在圣彼得和保罗教堂被洗礼. 7岁时,路德进入了曼斯菲尔德拉丁学校. 他在那里学习了拉丁语的语法和祷告,并记住了艾索普的"寓言".
featured.title_zh: 马丁·路德的5个拉丁短语
featured.content: Martin Luther was born in Eisleben, Germany, on November 10, 1483. He was christened at Saints Peter and Paul Church the next day. At age 7, Luther entered the Mansfeld Latin School. There he learned Latin grammar and prayers, and he memorized Aesop’s Fables . From those early years through his time studying at boarding school in Magdeburg then later at the University of Erfurt, Luther was a diligent student. He kept up with his Latin, and several important Latin phrases appear throughout Luther’s writings. Five of them serve as a good summary of his life and chief theological emphases. 1. Iustitia Dei In July 1505, Luther was caught in a fierce thunderstorm. Panicked and terrified, he bargained with God, promising to become a monk. After entering the monastery, Luther was again overcome by fear. When he led his first mass as a priest, it wasn’t an occasion of joy. Instead, it was filled with trembling. As the service began, Luther took his place at the front of the chapel, and he began to recite the Latin prayers. Luther knew that God is perfect in judgment and completely without sin. So as he thought about iustitia Dei , “the righteousness of God” (Rom. 1:17), terror struck him. Biographer Roland H. Bainton describes the thoughts that plagued Luther’s mind: Who am I that I should . . . raise my hands to the divine Majesty? The angels surround him. At his nod the earth trembles . . . [but] I am dust and ashes. When Luther held up the bread and wine, he shook so badly he almost dropped the cup. During those years growing up in school and at the monastery, Luther only thought of God’s righteousness, or justice, as his active judgment against human sin. He later wrote , Though I lived as a monk without reproach, I felt and knew I was a sinner before God. I had an extremely disturbed conscience. . . . I hated the righteous God who punishes sinners. 2. Extra nos In 1512, Luther became a university professor in Wittenberg. As he studied the Bible for his lectures, he began to see God’s righteousness in a new light. Luther saw how Jesus Christ took on our humanity, how he lived a perfect life and died the painful and shameful death of the cross to take the punishment due for sin. He saw how God raised Jesus from the dead, and how he now justifies Christians by faith. God declares that in his sight, Jesus’s perfect life and sacrificial death count for all believers. So God’s righteousness isn’t merely his judgment. It’s also his gift of salvation. Jesus’s perfect life and sacrificial death count for all believers. So God’s righteousness isn’t merely his judgment. It’s also his gift. What happened when Luther made this discovery? Here’s how he described it: “I felt that I was altogether born again and had entered paradise itself through open gates.” After that day, Luther began to teach that God gives Christians his “alien righteousness,” that is, a righteousness that comes extra nos , “from outside of us.” Our righteousness isn’t from us; it doesn’t come from what we do. It can’t be earned by saying a prayer or even by having a good attitude. Our righteousness is ultimately found in and belongs to another, our Savior Jesus Christ. 3. Crux sola est nostra theologia On October 31, 1517, Luther famously posted his Ninety-five Theses on the door of Castle Church. In it, Luther spoke clearly against the money-raising indulgence schemes Pope Leo X and Germany’s own Prince Albert of Brandenburg had sponsored. The next year, in April 1518, Luther defended these views at the Augustinian order’s spring meeting in Heidelberg. Luther walked to the meeting in fear. He expected the leaders there to sternly rebuke him. After all, that’s what the pope had asked them to do. But to Luther’s surprise, the leaders at the meeting welcomed his defense with excitement. What did Luther say that got his new friends so excited? In his Heidelberg Disputation , Luther described two types of people—the “theologian of glory” and the “theologian of the cross.” Theologians of glory think people are capable and smart enough to know God through human reason. They also say we can know who God’s righteous people are because we see God reward them with political power, success, and wealth. Though Luther didn’t use Albert’s and Leo’s names in his disputation, it’s clear he was talking about their greedy doctrine of indulgences when he described the theologian of glory. Luther’s “theologian of the cross,” by contrast, knows it’s not always people who appear good, beautiful, and powerful by worldly standards who truly know God. After all, Jesus didn’t look glorious on the cross. “One deserves to be called a true theologian,” Luther wrote , “who sees God even in suffering.” As Paul wrote, “God chose what is foolish in the world to shame the wise; God chose what is weak in the world to shame the strong” (1 Cor. 1:27). After Heidelberg, the phrase “ Crux sola est nostra theologia ” (“The cross alone is our theology”) became a rallying cry for Luther’s followers. It still is today. 4. Oratio, meditatio, tentatio Luther’s teaching set the Protestant Reformation in motion. In support of his reforms, Luther published hundreds of books, sermons, and hymns. Significantly, he also translated the entire Bible into the language of Germany’s common people. But Luther didn’t want common people to merely read Scripture. He wanted them to study it too. In the 1539 preface to the Wittenberg edition of his German writings, Luther wrote, “God himself lives in the Bible. Therefore, worthy Christian: get in, get in!” Luther gave his readers three rules for digging into God’s Word. Each has its own Latin term: prayer ( oratio ), meditation ( meditatio ), and suffering ( tentatio ). A ‘theologian of the cross’ knows it’s not always people who appear good, beautiful, and powerful by worldly standards who truly know God. The first rule is kept before we read the Bible. Luther wrote, “Kneel down in your private room and with humility, pray to God to give you his Holy Spirit to enlighten and guide and give you understanding.” The second rule is kept while reading: “Read and reread the very words written down in the Bible. Observe and think about what the Holy Spirit means.” The last rule is kept when we practice what the Scriptures say. Luther said, As soon as you begin to know God’s word, the devil will afflict you. . . . This suffering will teach you how right, true, sweet, lovely, mighty, and comforting God’s word is. It is wisdom supreme. 5. Simul iustus et peccator Luther was zealous and driven. He once said, “When I want to compose, write, pray, and preach well, I must be angry.” But while anger may have given Luther energy for work, it too often burned out of control. Sadly, today, Luther is as famous for his harsh words spoken against his enemies and the Jews as he is for recovering the biblical doctrine of justification. Throughout his life, Luther taught that believers are simul iustus et peccator . That’s Latin for “simultaneously justified and a sinner.” Both realities are true of every Christian. Both were true of Luther. He was a broken man who desperately needed God’s grace, and he knew it. Luther died while visiting Eisleben on February 18, 1546. Before he died, Luther scribbled out his last written words: “We are beggars. This is true.” Luther knew he could never earn God’s grace. Salvation isn’t won through indulgences or daily prayers. This is what Luther had discovered from the Bible and taught again to the world. God sent his only Son. Christ has overcome the world. All he asks of poor, begging sinners is that we believe.

马丁·路德于1483年11月10日生于德国艾斯莱本. 第二天他在圣彼得和保罗教堂被洗礼. 7岁时,路德进入了曼斯菲尔德拉丁学校. 他在那里学习了拉丁语的语法和祷告,并记住了艾索普的"寓言".
从早年到后来在马格德堡的寄宿学校学习,路德是一名勤奋的学生。 他跟上了拉丁语,几个重要的拉丁语短语也出现在路德的著作中. 其中5个是他的生平和首席神学重心的良好总结. 1. 联合国
1505年7月,路德被猛烈的雷暴所困. 惊慌惊恐地与上帝讨价还价,许诺成为和尚. 进入修道院后,路德再次被恐惧所克服. 当他第一次作为牧师主持弥撒时, 相反,充满了颤抖。
随着礼拜的开始,路德在礼拜堂前取而代之,他开始背诵拉丁语祈祷. 路德知道上帝在判断上是完美的,并且完全没有罪恶. 因此,当他想到了iustitia Dei“上帝的公义”(1:17)时,恐怖袭击了他。 传记作者罗兰·H·班顿(Roland H. Bainton)描述了困扰路德思想的思想:我应该是谁?
举起手来见圣上? 众天神围绕他. 在他点头的时候,大地会颤抖... ...但是,我是灰尘和灰烬。 当路德拿起面包和葡萄酒时,他摇得这么厉害,差点把杯子掉下. 在那些年里,路德在学校和修道院里长大,他只把上帝的正义或正义视为他对人类罪恶的积极判断。
他后来写道, 虽然我作为一个和尚生活 没有责备, 我感觉和知道我是上帝面前的罪人。 我有一个极度不安的良心。 我憎恨惩罚罪人的善良之神 2. 1512年,路德成为维滕贝格的大学教授. 当他为他的演讲而学习圣经时,他开始在新的光芒下看到上帝的正义.
路德看到耶稣基督如何对待我们的人性,他如何过上完美的生活并死于十字架上的痛苦而可耻的死亡来取取罪的惩罚. 他看见了上帝如何使耶稣从死地复活,以及他现在如何通过信仰为基督徒辩护. 上帝宣布,在他看来,耶稣的完美生活和牺牲的死亡对所有信徒都很重要。
因此上帝的正义不仅仅是他的判断。 这也是他的救赎天赋。 耶稣的完美生活和牺牲的死亡是所有信徒的计数. 因此上帝的正义不仅仅是他的判断。 这也是他的天赋。 当路德做出这个发现时发生了什么?
他是这样描述的 : “ 我感到我再次出生,并通过开放的大门进入了天堂。 ” 在那一天之后,路德开始教导上帝给予基督徒“外星人的正义 ” , 即“来自我们以外的”一种格外不义的正义。 我们的正义不是来自我们,
祈祷, 我们的正义最终被发现 并属于另一个,我们的救主耶稣基督。 3. Crux sola est nostra Godologia 1517年10月31日,路德将他的"95个本事"出名地贴在了城堡教堂的门上.
路德在书中明确表示反对教皇利奥十世和德国自己的勃兰登堡阿尔贝特亲王赞助的集资宽恕计划。 次年,即1518年4月,路德在海德堡举行的奥古斯丁会令春季会议上为这些观点辩护. 路德在恐惧中走去开会. 他期望那里的领导人严厉斥责他。
这毕竟是教皇要求他们做的。 但令路德惊讶的是,与会领导人激动地欢迎他的辩护. 路德怎么说 他的新朋友这么兴奋?
路德在他的"海德堡争论"中描述了两类人——"荣耀之神"和"十字架之神". 荣耀的神学家们认为,人的能力和智慧足以通过人类理性来认识上帝. 他们也说,我们可以知道上帝的善良人民是谁,因为我们看到真主以政治力量、成功和财富奖励他们。
虽然路德在争论中并没有使用阿尔伯特和利奥的名字,但很明显,当他描述荣耀的神学家时,他在谈论他们贪婪的宽恕理论。 相对而言,路德的“十字架神学家”知道,并非总能让世界标准显示良好、美丽和强大的人真正了解上帝。 毕竟耶稣在十字架上并不光荣。
路德写道 : “ 一个人应该被称为真正的神学家,” 路德写道,“谁在痛苦中看到上帝。 ” 正如保罗所写道的:“上帝选择了世界上的愚蠢来羞辱智者;上帝选择了世界上的弱者来羞辱强者。” 海德堡之后, " Crux sola est nostra Godologia " ( " 十字架是我们的神学 " )成为路德信徒的呼声。
今天还是这样。 4. Oratio、meditatio、tentatio Luther的教义使新教改革运动开始。 为支持他的改革,路德出版了上百本书,布道,并作"赞". 重要的是,他还将整个"圣经"翻译成了德国普通人的语言. 但路德并不想普通人只读圣经。 他希望他们也研究它。
路德在他的德文著作"维滕贝格"1539年版的前言中写道:"上帝自己活在圣经中. 因此,值得的基督徒:上车,上车!” 路德给了读者三条钻入上帝之道的规则. 每个词都有自己的拉丁名词:祷告(oratio),冥想(meditatio)和苦难(tentatio).
一个“十字架的神学家”知道,并非总有人以世界标准看起来是好人、美丽人和强大的人真正了解上帝。 第一条规则在我们读出"圣经"之前被保留.
路德写道:“跪在你的私人房间里谦逊地祈祷真主赐予你他的圣灵以启蒙、引导和谅解。” 第二条规则在读取时保留:“读取并重读圣经所写的文字。 观察并思考圣灵的意义。” 最后一个规则是当我们实践圣经所说的话时,
路德说,一旦你明白上帝的话,恶魔就会折磨你。 这种痛苦将教你如何正确、真实、甜蜜、可爱、强大并安慰上帝的话。 这是智慧至上。 5. Simul iustus et peccator Luther是狂热和有动力的。
他曾经说过:“当我想写作、写作、祈祷和讲道的时候,我一定生气了。” 但是,虽然愤怒可能已经让路德精力充沛地工作,但是它经常被烧得失控. 可悲的是,今天,路德以其对敌人和犹太人的严酷言辞而出名,如同他收复了圣经中的辩解学说而出名.
路德一生教导信徒们, 这在拉丁语中是“极端合理和有罪者 ” 。 每个基督教徒都一样 路德也一样 他是一个破碎的人,他迫切需要上帝的恩惠,他知道这一点。 1546年2月18日路德在访问艾斯莱本时去世.
在他死前,路德写出他最后的文字:“我们是乞丐。 这是事实。” Luther知道他永远得不到上帝的恩惠。 救赎不是通过宽容或日常祈祷而赢得的。 这是路德从圣经中发现的,并再次向世界传授. 上帝派他唯一的儿子 基督战胜了这个世界 他只要求贫穷 乞求罪人 我们相信

featured.title: ‘Mosquito Bowl’: Football Stars on the Front Lines
featured.summary: Peter Berg’s ‘The Mosquito Bowl’ is essentially ‘Friday Night Lights’ meets ‘Hacksaw Ridge.’
featured.summary_zh: Peter Berg's The Mosquito Bowl本质上是周五夜光会合哈克锯脊。 这是一部与"周五夜光"(Gritty handhip camera, muted color paget, Sky后摇滚乐中的爆炸)相同的创意氛围的电影, 也与伯格的"星期五夜光"(The Mosquito Bowl (现在在剧院出演; 11月25日来到Netflix))一样,
featured.title_zh: “蚊子碗” ：前线的足球明星
featured.content: Peter Berg’s The Mosquito Bowl is essentially Friday Night Lights meets Hacksaw Ridge . It’s a movie with the same creative vibe as Friday Night Lights (gritty handheld camera, muted color palette, Explosions in the Sky post-rock soundtrack) but applied to a brutally violent true story of WWII’s Battle of Okinawa, one of the single bloodiest battles of the 20th century. Also like Berg’s Friday Night Lights , The Mosquito Bowl ( out now in theaters ; coming to Netflix November 25) is based on a book by Pulitzer Prize–winning journalist Buzz Bissinger . The 2022 book—subtitled A Game of Life and Death in World War II —only has one chapter (of 41) devoted to the actual 1944 football game dubbed “The Mosquito Bowl.” Most of the book is about the war, and the young men who left wives, kids, and promising NFL careers to fight it. Likewise, Berg’s film adaptation is mostly a somber, unflinching WWII film, with a brief reprieve of joy in the form of a football game on Guadalcanal between the 4th and 29th regiments of the 6th Marine Division. Just as in Friday Night Lights , where the drama of high school football parallels the struggles and triumphs of life off the field, the football game in The Mosquito Bowl parallels the “game of life and death” that surrounds the men at war. Sports are interesting in this way: They provide escape from real life but also training for it, an arena of danger and high stakes but not ultimate stakes. Sports often map onto life—we draw up plans and plays but have to improvise; we get hurt but can heal; we thrive individually through teamwork; sometimes we win and sometimes we lose. Yet sports are unlike real life too. Winning or losing on the field is a matter of trophies and glory, but off the field, it can be a matter of life and death. Young Men Willing to Fight and Die The Mosquito Bowl (rated R for graphic war violence and language), opens with a well-known epigraph from Herbert Hoover : Older men declare war. But it is youth that must fight and die. And it is youth who must inherit the tribulation, the sorrow, and the triumphs that are the aftermath of war. This is a movie about youth—or rather, the passage from youth into adulthood that war accelerates. This is a movie about youth—or rather, the passage from youth into adulthood that war accelerates. The movie opens with muddy college football scenes in the fall of 1941, as the four central characters are introduced: John McLaughry (Nicholas Galitzine), Brown quarterback; Bob Baumann (Bill Skarsgård), University of Wisconsin tackle; Tony Butkovich (Ray Nicholson), Purdue fullback; and Dave Schreiner (Tom Francis), Wisconsin end. They were all-star athletes with promising futures. Many of them were collegiate All-Americans and drafted by NFL teams. Yet December 7, 1941, happened, and their futures were all changed. Once bound together by football skill, friendly rivalry, and fierce competition on the gridiron, these men soon bonded in a different setting: as marines in WWII’s savage Pacific theater. Instead of fighting for yards on the field, they fought for ground in a war of attrition on Okinawa. Instead of a football in hand, they carried guns and bayonets. Instead of tackling their opponents, they wrestled them to the death in hand-to-hand combat. Like many in the Greatest Generation, these men volunteered to enlist and fight. The Mosquito Bowl celebrates their duty and sacrifice. In one scene, Baumann’s younger brother says, “You don’t have to go,” to which Baumann replies, “I do. I’m needed.” It’s hard to imagine star athletes, whether collegiate or professional, volunteering to go to war in 2026. But in 1943, it was normal. Okinawa, Bissinger writes in the book, was “by far the largest collection of athletes ever to die in a single battle.” And in the entirety of WWII, 21 NFL players died in combat, as well as two players from Major League Baseball. Why were they so willing to lay down their lives? Perhaps back then, men had the bigger horizon more in view. Life isn’t about serving oneself. It’s about serving others, fighting for things bigger than personal fulfillment. As Dave Schreiner tells John McLaughry, “This is us sacrificing for the unborn. What other real thing is there? What’s the point in all of this if it’s not for passing something on?” Numbed by War-Movie Violence The Mosquito Bowl honors the Greatest Generation and is commendable in its straightforward embrace of manly virtues like duty and sacrifice. But I disliked several aspects of the film. One is the language. I realize wartime soldiers in every era tend to be prolific in their employment of profane language. But even if men in the 1940s were as creative with the f-word as they are in this movie, is it really essential to the movie? It makes the film much less likely to be watched by families, which is a shame because it’s the sort of thing dads might want to watch with their younger sons. I also wish Berg had given less screen time to bloody battles and more time to quieter character moments and the titular football game. I get that it’s important to underscore the savage bloodbath that was the Pacific theater, and I get that the joyful escape of football is most pronounced when juxtaposed with the horrific realities of war. But it’s hard for contemporary war movies to viscerally depict the “war is hell” experience after the genre has been so saturated. Edward Berger’s adaptation of All Quiet on the Western Front (2022) felt like the final word on war-movie blood and guts. We’ve become numb to watching bodies get mangled every which way. Going forward, movies about savage warfare probably need to take a different approach. There are ways to capture battle horror without showing every gruesome detail. Furthermore, the desaturated, shaky-camera, chaotic choreography of war movies has become clichéd. I checked out a bit during these prolonged battle scenes. At times, it felt like Berg was inspired by Terrence Malick’s Guadalcanal movie, The Thin Red Line (one of the best war movies of all time). But what made Malick’s film so effective is that it employed violence only in a few intense, lyrical sequences, juxtaposed with long stretches of more contemplative material and tender character moments. The experience of war is important to capture accurately. But a war film becomes great when the meaning of war is also a focal point. Clint Eastwood’s WWII diptych, Flags of our Fathers and Letters from Iwo Jima (2006), strikes this balance well. The action-to-reflection ratio is not quite right in The Mosquito Bowl . Football as Far as the Curse Is Found The high point of Berg’s movie is the Mosquito Bowl game, even though it occupies too little of the overall runtime. In a movie that is rather bleak thematically and visually, the game provides a much-needed moment of joy for the characters and audience. Hosted as a morale booster for soldiers who would soon be sent to fight on Okinawa, the game (broadcast on the “mosquito radio network”) was set up to be “two-hand touch” only but quickly devolved into full-on tackle. Some of the guys wore Santa hats. There were big smiles, laughs, playful rivalry: young men allowed to be boys again. Here’s how Bissinger describes it in the prologue of his book: For roughly two hours the Mosquito Bowl wasn’t simply a reminder of what life had once been like for the players, but freedom and abandon, with the spectators captured in the same moment, screaming their heads off, whether drunk or sober. The beauty of sports, the ultimate power of it to carry you away, had never been stronger. But the scene is also bittersweet, for we know it’s not reality. Real life is harsh. Okinawa looms. Many of these boys playing football on Christmas Eve 1944 won’t live to see Christmas Eve 1945. This scene reminded me of the resonant poetry of Friday Night Lights , which depicted football in much the same way: youthful vibrancy and freewheeling joy, but tempered by the painful pressures

Peter Berg's The Mosquito Bowl本质上是周五夜光会合哈克锯脊。 这是一部与"周五夜光"(Gritty handhip camera, muted color paget, Sky后摇滚乐中的爆炸)相同的创意氛围的电影,
也与伯格的"星期五夜光"(The Mosquito Bowl (现在在剧院出演;11月25日来到Netflix))一样,
2022年的一书——被取名为"二战中生死的游戏"(A Game of Life and Death in World War)——只有一章(第41章)专门讲述了1944年被誉为"蚊子碗"的实际足球比赛. 这本书大多是关于战争的,而那些离开妻子,孩子的年轻人,以及有前途的NFL职业来对抗战争.
同样地,伯格的电影改编作品大多是一部默默无闻的WWII电影,以第6海军陆战队第4团和第29团在瓜达尔卡纳尔(Guadalcanal)上进行足球比赛的形式短暂地延缓了欢乐.
就像星期五的"夜光"一样,高中足球的戏剧与场外生活的斗争和胜利平行,"蚊子碗"(The Mosquito Bowl)的足球比赛与围攻战中男子的"生死游戏"平行. 体育是有趣的: 它们提供了逃避现实生活的机会,但也为它提供了培训,这是一个危险和利害攸关的场所,但不是最终利害攸关。
体育常常描绘在生活中——我们制定计划和玩法,但必须即兴发挥;我们受到伤害,但可以治愈;我们通过团队精神而单独地繁荣;有时我们赢,有时我们输。 然而,体育也不同于现实生活。 取胜或输于地是道道是道是道是道是道是道是道是道是道是道是道是道是道是道是道是道是道是道是道是道是道是道是道是道是道是道.
年轻人愿意战斗并死亡 蚊子碗(以平面战争暴力和语言评分为R),以赫伯特·胡佛出道的著名史诗":老人宣战"开场. 但是,青年必须战斗并死亡。 而正是青年必须继承三难之地,悲伤之地,而胜利之地是战争后遗症.
这是一部关于青年的电影, 这是一部关于青年的电影, 电影以泥地大学足球场景于1941年秋季开拍,因为四个中心人物被介绍:约翰·麦克劳克里(英语:John McLaughry (Nicholas Galitzine)),布朗四分卫;
鲍勃·鲍曼(英语:Bill Skarsgård),威斯康辛大学钓鱼台;托尼·布特克维奇(英语:Ray Nicholson),普杜克·全后卫;戴夫·施雷纳(英语:Dave Schreiner (Tom Francis)),威斯康辛大学终点. 他们是全明星运动员 前途光明 其中多为全美联队,由NFL球队起草. 然而1941年12月7日,却发生了,他们的未来都变了.
这些人一度被足球技巧、友好竞争和激烈的竞争捆绑在一起,但很快却在不同的环境下被束缚在一起:作为海军陆战队员在二战期间的野蛮太平洋剧场。 在冲绳的一次自然减员战争中,他们不是在战场上为码而战,而是为地而战. 他们没有手持足球,而是携带了枪和刺刀.
他们不但没有对付对手,反而用手相搏的方式将对手摔倒至死. 和"最伟大的一代"中的许多人一样,这些人自愿入伍并出战. 蚊子碗会庆祝他们的职责和牺牲. 在一个场景中,鲍曼的弟弟说,“你不必去,”鲍曼回答说,“我愿意。
需要我。 很难想象明星运动员, 但是在1943年,这是正常的. Bissinger在书中写道,冲绳是“迄今为止在一次战斗中死亡的运动员人数最多的集合地”。 而在整个二战中,有21名NFL球员在战斗中丧生,还有来自主力联赛棒球的两名球员.
为什么他们这么愿意牺牲自己的生命? 也许那时,男人的视野更大 生活不是为自己服务。 而是为他人服务, 正如Dave Schreiner告诉John McLaughry的那样,“这是我们为未出生的人而牺牲。 还有什么真实的?
如果不是为了传递东西, "蚊子碗"以战争电影"暴力"(War-Movie Violence The Mosquito Bowl)为荣,以直截了当地拥抱"责任"和"牺牲"等人性美德而著称. 但我不喜欢电影的几个方面。 一是语言.
我意识到每个时代的战时士兵在使用污名语言方面往往很繁多. 但是,即使20世纪40年代的男性对"f-word"的创造力和这出电影中的一样,这是否真的对电影至关重要? 这让影片不太可能被家人看,
我也希望伯格给 较少的屏幕时间 对于血腥的战斗 更多的时间 安静的角色时刻 和三角足球比赛。 我理解强调太平洋剧场的野蛮流血很重要,
但当代战争电影很难直截了当地描绘出"战争就是地狱", Edward Berger在"西部战线"(2022年)上改编的"All Quiet"(All Quiet on the Western Front (2022年)),感觉就像战争-电影"血和胆"上的最后一句话. 我们对看尸体被打乱已经麻木了。
向前看,关于野蛮战争的电影可能需要采取不同的做法。 有一些方法捕捉出战斗恐怖而不展示出每一个可怕的细节. 此外,战争电影的不饱和、摇摇欲坠、杂乱无章地编舞也成了陈词滥调。 我在这些漫长的战斗场景中检查了一下
贝格有时觉得受到特伦斯·马利克出演的瓜达尔卡纳尔电影"瘦子红线"的启发(这是有史以来最好的战争电影之一). 但马利克的影片之所以如此有效, 是因为影片只使用几起激烈的、充满诗意的相接相接的暴力事件,
战争的经验对于准确捕捉是重要的. 但当战争的意义也成为焦点时,战争电影就变得伟大了. Clint Eastwood的二战Diptych, 我们父亲的旗帜和来自硫磺岛的信件 (2006年) 很好地实现了这种平衡。 《蚊子碗》中的动作-反射比并不完全正确。
足球如被诅咒所发现 Berg的电影的顶点是"蚊子碗"(Mosquito Bowl)游戏,尽管它占据了整个跑步时间太少. 在一部相当暗淡的主题和视觉电影中,游戏为角色和观众提供了非常需要的快乐时刻.
游戏(在“Mosquito电台网络”上广播)的制作只是“双手触摸”, 有些家伙戴了圣诞老人帽子。 曾有"大笑","取笑","玩弄相争":青年男子允许再做男孩.
以下是Bissinger在书前所描述的: 蚊子碗在大约两小时的时间里, 体育的美丽, 其最终的力量 把你带走, 从来没有更强大。
因为我们知道这不是现实。 现实生活很严酷 冲绳开始出现。 许多人在1944年平安夜踢足球, 这个场景让我想起周五"夜光"(Friday Night Lights)的回响性诗歌,这些诗歌以同样的方式描绘了足球:青春的活力和自由转动的快活,但被痛苦的压力所缓解.

featured.title_zh: 牧师，抓住机会
featured.content: My coffee had gone cold as the church planter mourned that his church felt stagnant. Worse than not growing—a thick malaise had settled over the congregation. The first three years were exciting; the community was intrigued by a new church plant, genuinely curious about what it was all about. But everything had plateaued. Leaders grew complacent. Sundays—even with strong preaching—felt cold and passionless. The church’s reason for existing had shrunk to feeding and caring for the Christians who already called it home. The church planter couldn’t see how it was still transforming the community. An older mentor at the table cleared his throat. “I’m sorry to hear that. Let me ask you—what is one risky, hard thing the Lord is inviting your church to do that you’re hesitant to do?” The planter scratched his head. “I don’t know. I’ve never been asked that before.” The older man shrugged. “Every pastor should be ready to answer that question. If he can’t, he needs to spend some time praying and fasting until he can. Comfort and complacency are incredibly dangerous.” I’ve sat in enough of these conversations to know that wise, healthy risks are vital to the life of the church. Without them, the church atrophies. Its reason for existing collapses into self-care and, after a few years, into self-preservation. Risky and hard things keep gospel blood flowing through the body. Pastor, you cannot afford to coast. You cannot afford autopilot. You owe it to Jesus and to your church to make the most of opportunities in your city—which means that alongside preaching, teaching, praying, and developing leaders, you need to prioritize seeking new avenues for ministry. Be a gospel entrepreneur. Church-planting networks have long understood that entrepreneurial aptitude is essential for planters. But what about established churches—do their pastors need to be entrepreneurial too? What Is a Gospel Entrepreneur? There’s still hesitancy around saying pastors need entrepreneurial aptitude. Maybe it’s because we picture someone who constantly starts new things he can’t sustain—a person with a billion ideas who follows through on none of them. If this is what we mean, then no, we don’t want our pastors to be entrepreneurial. Comfort and complacency are incredibly dangerous. But a gospel entrepreneur is something different. He doesn’t pile up harebrained ideas. He stays awake and sober-minded about the opportunities the Lord is opening in the community. He sees the wooden frames of a new development and prays about how the gospel will reach those families once they move in. He looks at neighborhoods where existing churches can’t possibly reach everyone—and plants a church there. He saves, scrimps, and sacrifices to move a growing church plant into a more strategic location. He keeps his eyes open, his mind sharp, and his hands ready for the moment God opens a door. Biblical Call When this topic comes up, someone usually asks, “Where do you see the need for a pastor to be an entrepreneur in the Bible?” My answer often surprises people: Jesus’s parable of the dishonest manager. In Luke 16:1–9, a rich man discovers his property manager has been wasting his possessions and tells him to settle accounts—he’s about to be fired. The manager realizes losing his job means either digging or begging, so he immediately goes to work cutting deals to gain favor with other wealthy employers. When his employer finds out, he commends the manager for his shrewdness. Ethical or not, it was a genius move. At this point, we should ask, Why is Jesus telling this story? Maybe he’s about to indict people like the manager. But the manager’s dishonesty has nothing to do with Jesus’s point. The twist is that Jesus holds up the dishonest manager as an example of what he wants his disciples to be. “The master commended the dishonest manager for his shrewdness,” Jesus says. “For the sons of this world are more shrewd in dealing with their own generation than the sons of light” (Luke 16:8). The parable is, if anything, a lament. The world’s sons do a better job seizing opportunities to advance their kingdoms than we do in advancing Christ’s. The implication is sobering. The sons of light need to be as intentional and opportunistic about eternity as the world is about temporary gain. We need pastors who will prayerfully take risks, do hard things, feel the urgency, and grab opportunities. A gospel entrepreneur stays awake and sober-minded about the opportunities the Lord is opening in the community. Consider it this way. Walmart and Target already have plans for that empty lot next to the new development. Millions of dollars are being spent on demographic studies and marketing campaigns to grow somebody’s bottom line. Believe it or not, there’s probably a developer with more aggressive ideas for your church building than you have. I’ve even heard a story of a dying church in a small Colorado town that was slowly pushed out of its building—a local developer sent people to join as members, just so they could vote to sell. The sons of the world know how to expand their kingdoms. In the verses that follow the parable, Jesus connects the parable to faithfulness in little things, stewarding earthly resources well, and remembering that we serve God, not our budgets and assets. Our goal as pastors isn’t to keep our congregants happy, live off endowments, or maintain the institution’s favorite donors. Our job is to call people to pick up their crosses and follow Jesus into risky opportunities, where even if we die, people will see Jesus. Don’t Be Risk Averse The dishonest manager knew he had no time to be risk-averse or complacent. He had to seize every opportunity to save his own skin. Pastors and churches have no time to be risk-averse either—not for our own sake but for the gospel’s. Eternity is at stake. Pastor, be a gospel entrepreneur. When we stand before our Lord on the last day, may it not be true that the sons of the world had a greater influence on our community than we did.

我的咖啡凉了,因为教堂规划师哀悼 他的教堂感到停滞。 更糟糕的是,一种浓郁的疾病已经笼罩着整个会众。 头三年令人兴奋; 社区被一个新的教会工厂所吸引, 真正好奇的是它是什么。 但一切都已经稳定下来了 领导人越来越自满。
星期日,即使有强烈的传道,也感到寒冷而无激情。 教堂的存在原因已经缩小,以供养和照顾已经称之为家的基督徒。 教会规划师无法理解如何仍在改变社区。 餐桌上一位年长的导师清了喉咙. " 我很遗憾听到这个消息。
我问你,上帝邀请你的教会来做你犹豫不决的事,这有多么危险? 栽培者将他的头挠了. “我不知道。 我从来没有被问过。 长者作是灌顶. “每个牧师应准备回答这个问题。 如果做不到,他需要花一些时间祈祷和禁食,直到他能够。
舒适和自满是极其危险的。” 我受够了这些对话, 知道明智、健康的风险对教会的生活至关重要。 没有他们,教堂的奖杯。 它的存在原因陷入了自我护理,并在几年后陷入了自我保护. 冒险而艰难的东西使血流经身体 牧师,你负担不起海岸。
你买不起自动驾驶 你对耶稣和你的教会都有责任 在你的城市里充分利用机会 也就是说,除了传教、教义、祈祷和发展领袖之外,你需要优先考虑为部委寻找新的途径。 成为福音企业家. 教会植树网早就明白,创业能力对植树人至关重要。
但是,那些已经成立的教会——他们的牧师也需要创业吗? 福音企业家是什么? 牧师需要创业能力, 可能是因为我们想象有人不断发起新事物,
如果这就是我们的意思,那么不,我们不希望我们的牧师成为企业家。 舒适和自满是极其危险的。 但福音企业家却不同 他不会堆起后脑勺的想法。 他保持清醒和清醒的头脑 关于机会 上帝正在社区打开。
他看到新发展的木框,并祈祷一旦这些家庭搬入,福音会如何传入. 他看着周围的街道, 他为了把一个正在成长的教会植物迁入一个更具战略意义的地点而拯救了,施舍了,并做出了牺牲.
他睁开双眼,头脑锐利,手为上帝打开一扇门时刻做好准备. 圣经召唤 当这个话题出现时,人们通常会问:“你在哪里看到牧师在圣经中成为企业家的必要性?” 我的回答常常让人惊讶:耶稣以不诚实的经理为例。
在Luke 16:1–9中,一个富人发现他的地产经理在浪费他的财产,并告诉他结清账款——他即将被开除。 经理意识到失去工作意味着挖掘或乞讨,所以他立即去工作切割交易,以获得其他富有雇主的青睐. 当他的雇主发现后,他赞扬经理的狡猾.
道德与否,这是一个天才的举动。 此时此刻,我们应该问,耶稣为什么讲这个故事? 也许他即将起诉经理这样的人。 但经理的不诚实与耶稣的观点无关. 曲折之处在于耶稣举起不诚实的经理作为他想要他的门徒们成为什么的例子.
“主人称赞这位不诚实的经理的狡猾,”耶稣说。 “因为这个世界的儿子在处理自己的一代时比光明的儿子们更精明”(公爵16:8)。 譬喻如来所叹. 世界的儿子们比我们更能抓住机会推进他们的王国, 含义是清醒的。
光之子们需要像关于暂时收益的世界一样,是有意和机会性的。 我们需要牧师,他们将祈祷 冒险,做艰难的事情, 感受紧迫感,抓住机会。 一个福音的企业家 保持清醒和清醒的头脑 关于机会 主正在社区打开。 这样吧
Walmart和Target在新开发旁边已经计划了空地。 数百万美元用于人口研究和营销活动, 无论信不信, 可能有一个开发商 比你的教堂建筑更具有攻击性。
我甚至听到一个故事, 说科罗拉多州小镇的一座教堂正在死亡, 这座教堂被慢慢推出, 天下之子有能扩张其地之道.
在"比喻"之后的诗句中,耶稣将比喻与小事中的忠诚联系起来,妥善地管理地上的资源,并记住我们服务于上帝,而不是我们的预算和资产. 作为牧师,我们的目标不是让我们的教友们快乐,靠捐赠维持生活,或者维持该机构最喜爱的捐赠者。
我们的工作是号召人们拾起十字架,并跟随耶稣去冒险的机会,即使我们死了,人们也会看到耶稣. 不要规避风险 不诚实的经理知道,他没有时间反风险或自满。 他不得不抓住一切机会拯救自己的皮肤. 牧师和教会也没有时间回避风险,
永相危难. 牧师,做一个福音企业家。 当我们在最后一天站在我们的主面前时,也许世界的子孙对我们社会的影响比我们大。
